children: Brazil's federal tax authority has cut its forecast for revenue from a dividend tax introduced this year by nearly two-thirds, underscoring weaker-than-expected collections from a measure that had been expected to provide a significant boost to government coffers.

The new estimate is around 10 billion reais ($1.95 billion), down from an initial forecast of roughly 29 billion reais, Claudemir Malaquias, head of the tax revenue service Center for Tax and Customs Studies, told reporters on Tuesday. Collections from the tax have totaled 4.3 billion reais from January to August, he added.
